📡 Iran stands against an enemy with top military technology: Senior commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Coordinator of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari says Iran stands against an enemy possessing the world’s full range of equipment and technology, describing modern warfare as a battle of willpower and endurance.

Speaking at a ceremony honoring the Army’s top recruitment officers, Sayyari said Iran had successfully faced its enemies in recent wars as they failed to achieve their planned objectives.
​
The ceremony, held at the Army headquarters, focused on reviewing recruitment efforts and planning to attract more qualified personnel, particularly through the national university entrance examination.
​
During the event, the Army unveiled its comprehensive recruitment, selection and employment system, a third-generation system developed by the Human Resources Department using artificial intelligence.
​
The system allows personnel across the Islamic Republic of Iran Army to identify, recruit and ultimately attract talented candidates, while also providing online testing capabilities and being made available to all Army units.
​
Addressing the importance of recruiting high-quality personnel, Sayyari said, “The most important capital of any organization is its human resources, because people with qualitative characteristics can contribute to the growth of organizations.”
​
He added that human resources are also the most important element in strengthening the Army’s combat capabilities.
​
“Pure and faithful human resources can take us to our destination,” he said.
​
Sayyari said qualified personnel had enabled the Army to withstand the eight-year imposed war despite sanctions and continue fulfilling its primary mission of defending Iran’s territorial integrity and the Islamic Revolution.
​
Turning to recent imposed wars, Sayyari described the enemies’ failure to achieve their objectives as a success for Iran.
​
“We performed successfully in recent wars, and the reason was the enemy’s inability to achieve its planned objectives,” he said.
​
He also referred to the eight-year war with Iraq’s Ba’athist regime, saying the enemy had announced that it would capture Khorramshahr in one day and reach Tehran’s Azadi Square within seven days, but became trapped in Khorramshahr for 34 days.
​
“This means the failure of all the enemy’s strategies,” he said.
​
Sayyari said modern warfare was a battle of willpower and the ability to endure hardship, adding that Iran had performed very successfully in this regard.
​
“We must take pride in ourselves and know that today someone is standing against us who possesses all the equipment and technology of the world,” he said.
​
“We must hold our heads high that we have stood against such an enemy.”
​
The ceremony concluded with tributes to the Army’s recruitment officers from various sections.

🔻 Iranian, Indian judicial officials discuss cooperation on BRICS summit sidelines

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian and Indian judicial officials have held discussions on expanding bilateral and multilateral legal cooperation on the sidelines of a BRICS meeting of chief justices and senior judicial officials in New Delhi, with stronger judicial ties, arbitration and mediation emerging as key areas of focus.

Iran’s Judiciary Chief Ayatollah Gholam-Hossein Mohseni Eje’i is heading a high-ranking judicial and legal delegation attending the BRICS gathering, which brings together representatives from member and partner countries.
​
The meeting in New Delhi kicked off on Friday and is scheduled to continue through September 6.
​
According to India’s LiveLaw news website, Indian Supreme Court Chief Justice Surya Kant has held meetings with senior judicial officials from participating countries on the sidelines of the gathering.
​
Discussions have revolved on bolstering judicial cooperation and bilateral relations, as well as exploring potential agreements to institutionalize cooperation among participating countries.
​
The officials also examined the role of arbitration and mediation in resolving commercial and corporate disputes and discussed mechanisms that could facilitate cross-border business activities.
​
Efficient commercial courts and mutual recognition and enforcement of judicial decisions were highlighted as important measures for strengthening investor confidence and supporting international commerce.
​
The use of technology and artificial intelligence in judicial systems was another major topic, with atendees emphasizing digital tools to improve efficiency and accelerate judicial proceedings.
​
The Iranian delegation’s agenda includes bilateral meetings with judicial officials from BRICS countries, participation in specialized panels and working groups, and speeches at the opening and closing sessions.
​
The discussions also seek to promote judicial assistance, exchange legal expertise and strengthen cooperation against transnational organized crime and other emerging legal challenges among participating countries.

Many mainstream makeup brands contain heavy metals — and that’s a real concern. These substances are dangerous because they bioaccumulate, meaning they build up in your body over time, increasing in concentration far beyond what’s found in the environment.

Once inside your system, heavy metals can settle in fat cells and contribute to a range of health problems — from damage to circulatory and nerve tissues, to liver and kidney issues, gastrointestinal irritation, joint pain, and even tumor growth. They may also play a hidden role in chronic and unexplained illnesses.
